The phrase "my compounds are on top of each other" is a common expression in organic chemistry labs referring to Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) or column chromatography. When two compounds have very similar polarities, they travel at nearly the same rate on a TLC plate or through a column, causing their spots or bands to overlap—literally appearing "on top of each other." This makes separation and purification difficult. The other options do not fit this typical lab jargon: similar boiling points relate to distillation, optical rotations to chirality, and non-covalent bonding to aggregation.

Answer: D
